questions.prompt: In a diesel engine, what ignites the fuel?
options: A glow plug at all times
questions.explanation: Air is compressed until it is hot enough to ignite the injected fuel; diesels need no spark.

questions.prompt: When is fuel injected in a four-stroke diesel cycle?
options: At bottom dead centre of the power stroke
Near the end of the compression stroke
questions.explanation: Diesel fuel is injected near the end of the compression stroke.

questions.prompt: How many crankshaft revolutions does one complete four-stroke cycle take?
questions.explanation: Four strokes of the piston equal two revolutions of the crankshaft.

questions.prompt: Why are diesel engines generally heavier than gasoline engines?
options: They use cast iron pistons only
They must withstand higher combustion pressures and temperatures
questions.explanation: Higher combustion pressures and temperatures need a heavier construction.

questions.prompt: Why do diesel engines use higher compression ratios than gasoline engines?
options: To lower fuel use at idle only
To heat the air to combustion temperature
questions.explanation: A diesel relies on compression heat for ignition, so it needs a higher compression ratio.

questions.prompt: What is torque rise?
options: An increase in torque when the engine is lugged down from rated RPM
The rise in engine speed under load
questions.explanation: Torque rise is the increase in torque as the engine is lugged down from rated speed.

questions.prompt: What does 'stroke' describe?
options: The distance the piston travels from top dead centre to bottom dead centre
questions.explanation: Bore is the cylinder diameter; stroke is the piston travel TDC to BDC.

questions.prompt: Which component transfers the piston's reciprocating motion into rotary motion?
questions.explanation: The crankshaft converts reciprocating motion into rotary motion.

questions.prompt: Wet cylinder liners use O-rings to...
options: Control oil flow to the bearings
Seal the water jacket and prevent coolant leakage
questions.explanation: Wet liners are in contact with coolant, so O-rings seal the water jacket.

questions.prompt: Why do main and connecting rod bearings wear faster than the crankshaft?
options: They are made of softer metal
questions.explanation: Bearings are made of softer metal, so they are designed to wear and be replaced.

questions.prompt: What do thrust main bearings minimise?
questions.explanation: Thrust bearings limit the end-play of the crankshaft in the block.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the camshaft?
options: To control intake and exhaust valve operation
questions.explanation: The camshaft lobes open and close the intake and exhaust valves.

questions.prompt: What do valve rotators do?
options: Turn the valve to prevent excessive wear in one spot
questions.explanation: Rotators turn the valve so it does not wear in one spot.

questions.prompt: What is the job of the idler gear in the gear train?
options: To drive the water pump only
To keep the camshaft gear turning the same direction as the crankshaft gear
questions.explanation: The idler gear keeps the camshaft turning in the same direction as the crankshaft.

questions.prompt: What are timing marks on the gear train used for?
options: To align the gears for correct timing
questions.explanation: Timing marks align the gears so components stay synchronised.

questions.prompt: In the cooling system, heat always moves...
options: From the coolant into the engine
From a hot source to a cooler target
questions.explanation: Heat always moves from a hot source to a cooler target.

questions.prompt: What does the temperature regulator (thermostat) do?
options: Maintains the proper range of operating temperature by controlling coolant flow to the radiator
questions.explanation: The regulator is the 'traffic cop', sending coolant to the radiator only when needed.

questions.prompt: Why does a radiator cap keep the cooling system under pressure?
options: To raise the boiling point of the coolant
questions.explanation: Pressure raises the boiling point; the cap's valves release excess pressure and admit air when cooling.

questions.prompt: What antifreeze concentration range gives adequate protection without reducing heat removal?
questions.explanation: Below 30% gives inadequate protection; above 60% reduces heat removal and freeze protection and causes silica dropout.

questions.prompt: What can happen if coolant conditioner concentration is too low?
options: Cylinder liners corrode or suffer cavitation erosion
questions.explanation: Too little conditioner allows corrosion and cavitation erosion of liners.

questions.prompt: Why is water the main ingredient of coolant?
options: It transfers heat better than any other substance
questions.explanation: Water transfers heat better than any other substance; glycol and conditioner add protection.

questions.prompt: In a full flow oil filter system, how much of the oil passes through the filter?
questions.explanation: In a full flow system 100% of the oil goes through the filter.

questions.prompt: When does the oil filter bypass valve open?
options: When the pressure difference across the filter exceeds the valve spring force, e.g. a clogged filter or cold oil
questions.explanation: The bypass protects the engine from oil starvation when the filter is restricted.

questions.prompt: What does the Total Base Number (TBN) of an oil indicate?
options: The amount of alkalinity additive that neutralises acids
questions.explanation: TBN shows the alkalinity additive that neutralises acids formed in combustion.

questions.prompt: What does Viscosity Index (VI) measure?
options: A base oil's ability to resist viscosity change with temperature
questions.explanation: VI is the resistance to viscosity change as temperature changes.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an aftercooler?
options: To cool the intake air after it passes through the turbocharger
questions.explanation: Aftercoolers cool the air after the turbocharger compresses (and heats) it.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of air flow in a turbocharged aftercooled system?
options: Compressor, precleaner, air filter, intake manifold, aftercooler
Precleaner, compressor, air filter, intake manifold, aftercooler
Precleaner, air filter, compressor, aftercooler, intake manifold
Air filter, precleaner, aftercooler, compressor, intake manifold
questions.explanation: Air goes precleaner, filter, turbo compressor, aftercooler, then intake manifold.

questions.prompt: How do fuel filters differ from oil filters?
options: Fuel filters are after the injectors
Fuel filters have no bypass valve
questions.explanation: Unlike oil filters, fuel filters have no bypass valve, so dirty fuel never reaches the injectors.

questions.prompt: What is the correct fuel flow order in a pump and lines system?
options: Tank, injection pump, primary filter, transfer pump, nozzles
Tank, transfer pump, nozzles, final filter, injection pump
Tank, final filter, primary filter, injection pump, nozzles
Tank, primary filter, transfer pump, final filter, injection pump, high pressure lines, nozzles
questions.explanation: Fuel goes tank, primary filter, transfer pump, final filter, injection pump, high pressure lines, nozzles.

questions.prompt: What does the Cetane Index of a fuel measure?
options: Its ignition quality, which affects starting and acceleration
questions.explanation: Cetane Index measures ignition quality.

questions.prompt: What is high idle?
options: The maximum rpm the engine is allowed to run under no load
questions.explanation: High idle is the maximum no-load speed allowed by the governor.

questions.prompt: On an EUI (electronic unit injector) system, what replaces the mechanical governor, rack and timing advance?
questions.explanation: On EUI systems the ECM and sensors take over governing, timing and fuel ratio control.
